title: sweep() has no access control: any caller can send the vault's entire native balance to an arbitrary address
description: Discovery: MODIFIER-01 / AC-01 (sibling comparison). setFee and transferOwnership in the same contract chain use onlyOwner, but sweep(), the only function that moves native value out, has no guard. Base.sol Owned offers onlyOwner and it is simply not applied. Sweep also ignores balances[], so depositEth credits become unbacked.
root_cause: A value-moving function lacks the onlyOwner check that its siblings carry, and does not consult the per-user ledger.

harm.magnitude: 100% of the vault native balance in one call

exploit_trace: 1. Users call depositEth() and the vault holds N wei.
2. Attacker (any EOA, not owner) calls sweep(attacker).
3. to.transfer(address(this).balance) moves N wei to the attacker.
4. balances[] still shows each user's ETH credit but nothing backs it.

preconditions.text: vault holds a non-zero native balance

postconditions.text: ETH credits in balances[] are unbacked

postconditions_created: ETH credits in balances[] are unbacked

title: Single balances ledger for ETH and ERC20: ETH depositors can withdraw other users' tokens, and withdraw() has no ETH counterpart
description: Discovery: Cross-function state consistency (writers of balances). depositEth() and deposit() both credit balances[msg.sender], but withdraw() is the only debit and always pays the ERC20. Any ETH credit is therefore redeemable one-for-one as token units, with no check that the token was deposited. Inverse parity deposit/withdraw is broken for ETH (Module W).
root_cause: Two unrelated assets share one mapping, and the only debiting function pays out one of them.

harm.magnitude: up to the vault's whole token balance, for the same number of wei (recoverable via sweep)

exploit_trace: 1. Victims deposit 1,000,000 token units via deposit().
3. Attacker calls withdraw(1_000_000): the debit passes and token.transfer sends 1,000,000 token units to the attacker.
4. Attacker calls sweep(attacker) to recover the 1,000,000 wei; victims' tokens are gone.

preconditions.text: vault holds tokens deposited by others

postconditions.text: token balance below sum of token depositors' balances; totalDeposits wraps

postconditions_created: token balance below sum of token depositors' balances

title: withdraw() subtracts totalDeposits in an unchecked block although depositEth never increments it: counter wraps to ~2^256
description: Discovery: Module M (counter consistency) / Step 5b guard consistency. totalDeposits is raised only by deposit(), but lowered by withdraw() for any balances[] credit including ETH credit. The unchecked subtraction removes the 0.8 underflow revert, so the counter silently wraps and totalDeposits no longer reflects deposits. No in-scope code reads it for payouts, so direct fund loss is not shown; any integration or later upgrade reading totalDeposits gets garbage.
root_cause: Counter and ledger are updated by different paths and the debit is unchecked.

harm.who: integrators or off-chain consumers reading totalDeposits
harm.magnitude: totalDeposits wraps to near 2^256 after one ETH-credit withdrawal

exploit_trace: 1. totalDeposits = 0; user calls depositEth{value: 1 ether}(): balances[user] = 1e18, totalDeposits still 0.
2. If the vault holds tokens, user calls withdraw(1e18).

preconditions.text: withdraw() succeeds, i.e. vault holds enough tokens (see DA-2)

postconditions.text: totalDeposits permanently desynced from real deposits
